s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis
salient_findings: Reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
key_facts: Previous treatment with topical antifungal cream showed no improvement
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C serologic tests were negative

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis and histologic findings of vascular proliferation and hemosiderin deposits

shortlist.label: Hobnail hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similar histologic features of vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40, and presence of hemosiderin deposits

shortlist.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by similar vascular proliferation and presence of hemosiderin deposits, consistent with the patient's clinical and histologic findings

shortlist.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with similar clinical features of a gradually enlarging, asymptomatic skin lesion and histologic findings of vascular proliferation and spindle-shaped endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of a reddish-brown skin lesion and histologic findings of vascular proliferation and epithelioid endothelial cells, although less common than other options

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border, combined with the histologic findings of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation and prominent hemosiderin deposits, is consistent with targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma. The presence of promontory signs and the immunohistochemical profile also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hobnail hemangioma
rejected.why: While hobnail hemangioma can present with similar clinical features, the histologic findings and immunohistochemical profile in this case are more consistent with targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.

rejected.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
rejected.why: Glomeruloid hemangioma is typically associated with POEMS syndrome, which is not mentioned in the case, and the histologic findings do not match.

rejected.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
rejected.why: Spindle cell hemangioma typically presents with a distinct spindle cell component, which is not described in the histologic findings of this case.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
rejected.why: Epithelioid hemangioma typically presents with a more inflammatory appearance and a distinct epithelioid endothelial cell component, which is not described in the histologic findings of this case.
